previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of gastroparesis and a J-tube presented with a week-long episode of nausea and vomiting, consistent with a gastroparesis flare after years of good control. She was admitted for symptom management, during which she developed mild leukocytosis and transient diarrhea, but remained afebrile with no signs of infection. Imaging confirmed the J-tube was in place and functioning. She was treated with IV fluids, anti-nausea medications, and gradual advancement of diet. Her symptoms resolved, acidosis corrected, and she tolerated a regular diet. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue home medications, follow a low-fat diet, and follow up with her PCP to monitor white blood cell count.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  History of gastroparesis with worsening nausea and vomiting.  Has
J-tube in place.  Confirm J-tube placement.

COMPARISON:  Abdominal radiograph from ___.

FINDINGS:

Single frontal abdominal radiograph was obtained after injection of the J-tube
with radiopaque contrast material.  Tip of the J-tube projects over the
expected location of the distal duodenum/duodenaljejunal junction with
contrast opacification of the proximal jejunum.  The J-tube position does not
appear significantly different compared to the prior study.  Evidence of prior
mesh surgery in the left upper quadrant and surgical clips in the right upper
quadrant are noted.  Bowel gas pattern is nonobstructive.  

IMPRESSION:
Patent J-tube with tip in the distal duodenum/proximal jejunum with
opacification of the jejunum.
